review_notes: Read the whole file. Checked Mathlib for existing equivalents of the local definitions. Found Mathlib's MulSemiringAction.charpoly (Invariant/Basic.lean) and the Subgroup.mulSemiringAction instance. The local prodXSubSMulSubgroup is the same polynomial as charpoly H x when H acts on R by restriction, and its supporting lemmas mirror the Mathlib ones. I did not flag fixedSubringRamificationDepth or cosetRamificationDepthSum: they are specialisations of the project's own ramificationDepth, not Mathlib concepts. I did not flag addVal_finset_prod or the smul_aeval-style lemmas: they are theorem-level duplication, which the rubric excludes. findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def prodXSubSMulSubgroup (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] (x : R) : R[X] :=
  ∏ h : H, (X - C ((h : G) • x))
findings.problem: This is Mathlib's `MulSemiringAction.charpoly` for the finite group H, which acts on R through the existing `Subgroup.mulSemiringAction` instance. Mathlib's definition is `∏ g : G, (X - C (g • b))`. Taking G := H gives `∏ h : H, (X - C (h • x))`, and `h • x` is definitionally `(h : G) • x`. The file defines a competing polynomial and re-proves the matching API: evaluation at x is zero (cf. `eval_charpoly`), invariance under the group (cf. `smul_charpoly`), and invariant coefficients (cf. `smul_coeff_charpoly`). The new name, `smul_prodXSubSMulSubgroup`, and the hand-written `Fintype.prod_bijective` reindexing add a second vocabulary for the same object.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the local definition and use `MulSemiringAction.charpoly H x`, with `H` as the acting group. Keep `prodXSubSMulSubgroup` only as an `abbrev` or notation if the name is wanted. Replace `eval_prodXSubSMulSubgroup_self` with `MulSemiringAction.eval_charpoly`. Replace `smul_coe_prodXSubSMulSubgroup` and `coeff_prodXSubSMulSubgroup_mem` with `smul_charpoly` and `smul_coeff_charpoly`. Only the lemmas that translate between `(h : G) • x` and `h • x` for the coset-twisted evaluation (`smul_prodXSubSMulSubgroup`, `eval_smul_prodXSubSMulSubgroup`) and the divisibility lemma need to remain. `monic_charpoly` and `splits_charpoly` also come for free.
findings.benefit: Removes a duplicate definition and about three duplicated lemmas. Readers meet the standard Mathlib `charpoly` notion. Results about charpoly, such as `Algebra.IsInvariant.charpoly_mem_lifts`, apply directly instead of needing conversions.
